top_signal.title: Structuring a solo local inspection service in Guangzhou: How do I handle workflow and pricing without overcomplicating it?
top_signal.summary: Hi everyone,   Following up on my earlier post as an unemployed designer here in Guangzhou. Based on the great advice from this community, I decided to start a tiny solo business helping overseas buyers check samples at my local parcel station and scouting wholesale markets on the Guangzhou subway line (like Shisanhang for apparel, Sanyuanli for leather, Meibocheng for packaging, etc.).   As a first-time solo operator trying to set up my internal operations from scratch, I am struggling with three specific business structure questions and would love advice from experienced small business owners here:   First, when delivering a service report (like a sample unboxing video or a market walk-through), how do you balance speed vs. polish? As a designer, I tend to over-edit my PDFs and videos, which eats up too much time. What is the single most critical part of a deliverable that I should focus 80% of my energy on, and what administrative fluff can I cut out to improve my workflow?   Second, how do service businesses handle scope creep when doing local legwork? Since I am restricting my early practice runs strictly to Guangzhou subway wholesale markets to keep my overhead at zero, how do I set clear operational boundaries so a simple half-day scouting task doesn't turn into endless unpaid follow-ups?
